tasks.spec: You are a fleet health checker. Probe the Paperclip API at http://127.0.0.1:3100/api by running: curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:3100/api/issues?limit=1. Also probe Ringside at http://127.0.0.1:8700 and Bifrost at http://127.0.0.1:8078. Write a JSON report to ./health-report.json with keys: paperclip_status (string), ringside_status (string), bifrost_status (string), timestamp (ISO 8601), and all_ok (boolean, true only if all three returned 200). Do not modify any service. Boundary: read-only HTTP probes only.
tasks.check: python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(open('health-report.json')); assert d.get('paperclip_status')=='200', f'paperclip: {d.get(\"paperclip_status\")}'; assert d.get('ringside_status')=='200', f'ringside: {d.get(\"ringside_status\")}'; assert d.get('bifrost_status')=='200', f'bifrost: {d.get(\"bifrost_status\")}'; assert d.get('all_ok')==True; print('health-check OK: all services responding')"
tasks.verified: health-report.json confirms Paperclip, Ringside, and Bifrost all returned HTTP 200

tasks.spec: You are a fleet memory-plane health checker. Probe each memory plane and write results to ./memory-health.json. For each plane, run a curl health check and record the HTTP status or connection result: OB1 at http://127.0.0.1:8787 (GET /), Hindsight at http://127.0.0.1:8888 (GET /), Honcho at http://127.0.0.1:8005 (GET /v3/workspaces). The JSON must have keys: ob1 (string status or 'error: <msg>'), hindsight (string), honcho (string), all_healthy (boolean), timestamp (ISO 8601). Do not modify any service. Boundary: read-only HTTP probes only.
tasks.check: python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('memory-health.json')); assert d.get('ob1','').startswith('200') or 'ok' in d.get('ob1','').lower(), f'OB1 unhealthy: {d.get(\"ob1\")}'; assert d.get('hindsight','').startswith('200') or 'ok' in d.get('hindsight','').lower(), f'Hindsight unhealthy: {d.get(\"hindsight\")}'; assert d.get('honcho','').startswith('200') or 'ok' in d.get('honcho','').lower(), f'Honcho unhealthy: {d.get(\"honcho\")}'; print('memory-planes OK')"
tasks.verified: memory-health.json confirms OB1, Hindsight, and Honcho are all responding

tasks.spec: You are a fleet infrastructure checker. Run 'docker ps --format "{{.Names}} {{.Status}}"' and write the output to ./container-status.txt. Then run 'lsof -i :3100 -i :8700 -i :8078 -i :8787 -i :8888 -i :8005 -S' and append the output to the same file with a header line '---PORTS---'. Do not start, stop, or modify any container or port binding. Boundary: read-only inspection commands only.
tasks.check: test -s container-status.txt && grep -q 'NAMES' container-status.txt && grep -q 'PORTS' container-status.txt && echo 'container-status OK: docker ps and port bindings captured'
tasks.verified: container-status.txt contains docker container list and port binding output

tasks.spec: You are a fleet health summarizer. Read ./health-report.json, ./memory-health.json, and ./container-status.txt from your task directory. Synthesize them into ./health-summary.md with these sections: '# Fleet Health Summary', '## API Services' (table of service, status, healthy?), '## Memory Planes' (table), '## Container & Port Status' (key findings), '## Overall Status' (PASS if all_ok and all_healthy are true, otherwise FAIL with named failures). Include a timestamp. Do not probe services yourself — use only the input files. Boundary: read the three input files, write only health-summary.md.
tasks.check: test -s health-summary.md && grep -qiE '# Fleet Health Summary' health-summary.md && grep -qiE 'API Services|Memory Planes|Container|Overall' health-summary.md && echo 'summary OK'
tasks.verified: health-summary.md synthesizes all three probe results into a structured health report with an overall PASS/FAIL verdict
